newsitem.title: GERMANY: ECB forex intervention linked to convergence.
newsitem.headline: ECB forex intervention linked to convergence.

text.p: The European Central Bank will intervene in currency markets from time to time, but will only help non-Euro European currencies if their countries follow convergence policies, the European Monetary Institute said.

The EMI said in a report published on Monday that it was not yet decided whether the ECB would take a centralised or decentralised approach to intervention. Intervention could also take place on major non-European currencies such as the dollar.

"Such operations might be effected in order to influence exchange rate developments between the euro, on the one hand, and other EU currencies or non-EU currencies, e.g. the U.S. dollar, on the other," the report said.

In the EU context, it said, "intervention should be used only as a supportive instrument, in conjunction with other policy measures, including appropriate fiscal and monetary policies conducive to economic convergence and exchange rate stability within the EU."

The EMI, which as forerunner to the ECB is charged with drawing a blueprint for its policy tools and operations, said that preparatory work was being conducted to allow the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) to adopt either centralised or decentralised intervention policies.
Under a centralised policy, intervention operations would be carried out exclusively by the ECB, using its own technical infrastructure.
A decentralised system would mean that all participating national central banks would conduct intervention, following instructions from the ECB.
The intervention would be conducted using the up to 50 billion euros of reserves which will be transferred to the ECB by the national central banks, the EMI said.
